chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from al-Fudayl, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“The grave-robber, when he is known for that, has his hand cut off.”

key_terms.اَلنَّبَّاشُ: the one who digs up graves to steal from them
key_terms.قُطِعَ: his hand is cut off as the prescribed punishment
key_terms.مَعْرُوفًا: known or recognized as being characterized by the act

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a grave-robber in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the grave-robber. It states that when a person is known for this act, the punishment of amputation is applied, indicating the gravity of violating graves and committing theft in this manner.
